chunk_text: Pungent, saline, bitter, mixed, sweet, acidulous and astringent are respectively tastes lorded by the Sun etc.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: Strong in the east are Mercury and Jupiter. The sun and Mars are so in the south while Saturn is the only planet that derives strength in the west. The Moon and Venus are endowed with vigour when in the north.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: strong during night are the Moon, Mars and Saturn while Mercury is strong during day and night. The rest (i.e. Jupiter, the Sun and Venus) are strong only in day time.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: During the dark half malefics are strong. Benefics acquire strength in the bright half of the month.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: Malefics and benefics are respectively strong in Dakshinayana and Uttarayana.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: The lords of the year, month, day and Hora (planetary hour) are stronger than the other in ascending order.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: Again stronger than the other in the ascending are : Saturn, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, the Moon and the Sun.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: The directions of the planets may be understood as under: The Sun - east, Saturn - west, Venus - south-east, The Moon - north-west, Mars - south, Mercury - north, Jupiter - north-east, Rahu - south-west.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: The Sun rules strong trees (i.e. trees with stout trunks). Saturn useless trees, the Moon milky trees (like rubber yielding plants), Mars bitter ones (like lemon plants), Venus floral plants, Jupiter fruitful ones and Mercury fruitless ones.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: Rahu rules the outcaste while Ketu governs mixed caste.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: Saturn and the nodes rule anthills.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: Rahu denotes multi-coloured clothes and Ketu rags. Jupiter, the Sun, the Moon, Mercury, Mars and Saturn in their turn govern saffron, silken, red silken, white silken, black silken and multi-coloured robes. Other authorities hold the following view about planetary robes: The Sun - coarse, the Moon - new, Mars - burnt, Mercury - durable, Saturn - torn, Rahu - multi-coloured and Ketu - much torn.

chunk_text: Lead and blue gem belong to Rahu and Ketu respectively.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: Vasanta, Greeshma, Varsha, Sarad, Hemanta and Sisira are the six Ritus, or seasons, governed by Venus, Mars, Moon, Mercury, Jupiter and Saturn.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: Dhatu planets are Rahu, Mars, Saturn and the Moon while the Sun and Venus are Moola planets. Mercury, Jupiter and Ketu rule Jeevas.
meta_source_ref: BPHS1, Chapter 1 - PLANETARY CHARACTERS AND DESCRIPTION (Part 3)

chunk_text: Out of all the planets Saturn is the eldest (i.e. with the highest age). He bestows maximum number of years in Naisargika Dasa.

chunk_text: For the seven planets from the sun on, the signs of exaltation are respectively Aries, Taurus, Capricorn, Virgo, Cancer, Pisces and Libra.
